summary: CRITICAL FRONTEND BUG REPRODUCED: With admin auth via demo-login the V1 multi-transcript Connect Schedule UI (/admin/business-cases/:id/connect/schedule) now renders correctly — all expected data-testids present (business-case-flow-page, stepper-connect, connect-add-transcript-btn, connect-transcript-content-<sid>, connect-analyze-all-btn, connect-analysis-results). HOWEVER the frontend save loop (`saveConnectTranscriptSessions` at /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/V1BusinessCaseFlowPages.js lines 435-479) silently DROPS sessions whenever it has to create a NEW meeting for an unsaved session. With 4 transcripts filled (verified value.length=63 on all 4 textareas), the backend received only 3 POSTs and persisted only 2 transcripts (the third meeting was created with transcript_len=0; the 4th session never got POSTed at all). After navigate-away+return only 3 editors hydrate; after reload still 3. This is a regression in the multi-transcript save flow itself, NOT in the hydration code (the iter22 hydration fix lines 1001-1035 is correct — when the backend has N business_call meetings, the UI hydrates N editors sorted by date). The hydration test passes only if the save loop actually persists every session, which it does not. Backend pytest from iter22/iter23 remains GREEN (it bypasses the UI loop and POSTs each meeting directly via v3CreateMeeting+v3UploadMeetingTranscript with awaits — confirming backend is healthy). Anthropic still returns honest_fallback (out of credit balance) — acceptable per task brief.

ui_bugs.issue: When multiple transcript sessions have no meetingId (newly added in the UI without prior persistence), the for-loop at /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/V1BusinessCaseFlowPages.js lines 445-477 breaks after the FIRST v3CreateMeeting call. Observed sequence on a 4-session save (sessions 1+2 had prior meetingIds, sessions 3+4 did not): (a) POST /api/v3/meetings/<id1>/transcript OK, (b) POST /api/v3/meetings/<id2>/transcript OK, (c) POST /api/v3/meetings (creates new meeting for session 3) — but no subsequent transcript upload, and session 4 never starts. The newly created meeting persists with transcript=''. Net result: 2/4 transcripts saved; 1/4 created-but-empty; 1/4 lost entirely. Most likely cause is that v3CreateMeeting's response is missing or differently-keyed `id` so `meeting.id` is undefined → v3UploadMeetingTranscript(undefined, …) throws → for-loop bails out before the next iteration. Either the API client (v3CreateMeeting) is unwrapping the response wrong, or the backend create endpoint is returning the meeting under a different key (e.g. `meeting_id` or wrapped in `{data: …}`). Add a console-visible error log inside the catch and a fallback to read meeting.meeting_id / meeting.data?.id.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix saveConnectTranscriptSessions loop at /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/V1BusinessCaseFlowPages.js lines 445-477. The line `meetingId = meeting.id;` after v3CreateMeeting likely receives undefined for `meeting.id`. (a) Inspect v3CreateMeeting in the api client to confirm it returns the raw meeting object with an `id` field, and not a wrapper like {meeting: …}, {data: …}, or {meeting_id: …}. (b) Add `if (!meetingId) throw new Error('v3CreateMeeting returned no id: ' + JSON.stringify(meeting));` so the failure surfaces to the user instead of silently breaking. (c) Wrap each iteration in try/catch and collect partial-success vs failure counts so the save banner can report 'Saved 2 of 4 transcripts — 2 failed.'
Add a DELETE /api/v3/meetings/{id} endpoint so UI tests can self-clean without direct Mongo writes.

Surface backend save errors as a red toast in the UI instead of letting analyze-all silently run on a partial dataset (currently the user sees the 'AI analyser offline — safe fallback' banner and assumes everything is fine).

Once the save-loop fix lands, re-run the full Playwright regression: fill 4 transcripts → save → nav-away+return → expect 4 editors → append 5th → save → nav-away+return → expect 5 → reload → still 5. Also assert POSTs == 4 unique /api/v3/meetings + 4 unique transcript uploads on the first save.
critical_code_review_comments: saveConnectTranscriptSessions loop (lines 445-477) has NO try/catch. A single failed iteration drops all subsequent sessions silently. This is the root cause of the data-loss reproduced in this run. Wrap the body of the for-loop in try/catch and collect per-session results.

v3CreateMeeting response shape is implicit — the loop blindly trusts `meeting.id` exists. Add an assertion or a fallback unwrap (`meetingId = meeting?.id || meeting?.data?.id || meeting?.meeting?.id`) and surface a hard error if all are undefined.

saveConnectTranscriptSessions re-uploads transcripts for sessions that already had a meetingId on every save — write amplification still present (carried over from iter22/iter23). Skip the v3UploadMeetingTranscript call when content == previously-saved transcript.
V1BusinessCaseFlowPages.js at 4159 lines is far over the 700-line guideline; the Connect/Schedule/Questions/Analysis components and the save helper should live in a dedicated /admin/connect/ folder.

loadMeetings hydration (lines 1001-1035) is correct: filters by meeting_type=='business_call', sorts ascending by call_date/scheduled_for/created_at, de-dups by id, maps to sessions. The reason hydration appears 'broken' to a casual reviewer is that the SAVE loop persists fewer meetings than the UI displayed at click-time — the hydration only reflects what was actually saved.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (frontend save loop, NOT backend or hydration): saveConnectTranscriptSessions at /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/V1BusinessCaseFlowPages.js lines 445-477 iterates cleanSessions and, for any session without a meetingId, calls v3CreateMeeting then reads `meeting.id`. Observed behaviour with 4 sessions (2 hydrated with prior meetingIds, 2 newly-added): the loop successfully POSTs /transcript for sessions 1&2 (existing ids), then POSTs /api/v3/meetings for session 3 — but does NOT POST the subsequent /transcript and does NOT process session 4. The newly-created meeting persists with transcript=''. The most likely failure point is `meetingId = meeting.id;` returning undefined (v3CreateMeeting unwrapping the response wrong, e.g. returning `{data: meeting}` not the bare meeting, or the backend create endpoint returning the meeting under `meeting_id`/`_id` instead of `id`). The next line `await v3UploadMeetingTranscript(undefined, …)` throws (probably a 404 / type error), and because the for-loop has no try/catch the exception bubbles up to runCombinedAnalysis which catches it in setSaveNotice but the analyze-all has ALREADY started in parallel? No — actually analyze-all runs AFTER save (line 1110-1112), so analyze-all should never run if save throws. But the UI showed connect-analysis-results, so either save did NOT throw (returned partial savedSessions) or analyze runs despite the throw. REPRODUCTION: (1) seed admin auth, (2) goto /admin/business-cases/bc-472329ed4c/connect/schedule, (3) add 3 transcripts (4 total), fill content in all 4, (4) click Analyze All, (5) observe network: only 3 POSTs (2 transcript + 1 meeting), and only 2 transcripts persisted with content + 1 empty meeting + 1 lost. MITIGATION: (a) Add try/catch inside the for-loop body so a single failed session doesn't bail subsequent ones, (b) Add `meetingId = meeting?.id || meeting?.meeting_id || meeting?.data?.id` fallback unwrap, (c) Throw a hard 'No id returned from create' error if all unwraps fail so the bug surfaces immediately rather than silently dropping data, (d) Surface partial-failure as a visible red toast in setSaveNotice with the exact count of failed sessions. The iter22 hydration fix is correct and shouldn't be touched. Backend persistence is correct (10/10 pytest); the issue is purely in the UI save loop.
